exposure: mode of delivery (caesarean vs. vaginal for NICU admission)
cohort: The study included antenatal women admitted to the labour room with medical indications for induction of labour.
finding: The study identified several risk factors (age >30 years, non-vegetarian/mixed diet, primiparity, gestational age >40 weeks, Bishop score <5, BMI >25 kg/m2, and hypertensive disorders) significantly associated with an increased relative risk of caesarean delivery in induced labors.
mod_finding: The NICU admission rate was significantly higher in caesarean deliveries (43.1%) compared to vaginal deliveries (21.4%) (RR=2.01).
